title: Hover in the dap-view window evaluates the word under the cursor, not the tree node
description: With the cursor inside the Scopes tree, <leader>de evaluates vim.fn.expand('<cexpr>') against the rendered text of the tree line. On a Go session that text is a rendered value, so on the line 'Inner = main.Level2 {Inner: ma...' the cursor lands on the type name and delve answers 'Unable to evaluate expression: package main has no function Level2'. The error float then draws over the tree, which is how the user hit it. Same class of failure on Python, where the word under the cursor is a repr fragment rather than an expression.
design: actions.hover() falls back to util/exprs.get_current_expr(), which is expand('<cexpr>') in normal mode. The tree already carries what is needed: state.line_to_variable_path maps a line to a node path and state.variable_path_to_evaluate_name maps that path to the adapter's evaluateName. Branch on the current window being state.winnr (and on the current section being scopes or watches) and use that pair; fall back to the current behaviour only in a code window. The hover tree itself has the same pair under hover_path_to_*. Parent issue for the user-visible report in dv-kyf.
acceptance_criteria: Invoking hover while the dap-view window is the current window resolves the expression from the tree node under the cursor (its evaluateName), not from the buffer text. The type name of a rendered value is never sent to the adapter. Headless case under both hosts, and on a value whose rendering contains an identifier that is not a valid expression.

title: Hover on a large value (matrix) stalls and never shows a float
description: Hovering the 30x30 'matrix' variable takes a very long time and no float appears; the editor feels hung. Reproduced by the user on Go (dap-playground/go/main.go) and present in the Python fixture too, which has the same 30x30 matrix. Other variables on the same frame hover instantly, so it scales with the size of the value rather than being a fixed failure.
design: Suspects, in order. (1) hover/view.show measures width over the whole rendered value; a 30x30 matrix is thousands of cells and the float width computation plus nvim_win_set_width run per render. tree.max_value_width clamping (config default 60) may not be applied on the hover path at all, only in the scopes tree. (2) Expanding a 900-element array issues a variables request per level and renders every child. (3) The evaluate itself may be slow in delve for a large aggregate; if so, show the float first and fill it when the response lands rather than blocking. Measure before fixing: time the evaluate request separately from the render.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering any variable in the fixtures, matrix included, shows a float within a fraction of a second. Large values are clamped for display the way the tree already clamps them. The editor is never blocked while the adapter call is in flight. A headless timing assertion on the matrix value.

title: <leader>de hover float does not work in the user's Neovim
description: The eval-in-float hover, bound to <leader>de -> require('dap-view').hover(nil, true) in ~/.config/nvim/lua/plugins/dap.lua, does not produce a float in the user's own Neovim during a live debugpy session. QA's scripted runs of the same entry point passed, so the failure is specific to the real config or to invocation from a keymap rather than from RPC.
design: Suspects: the keymap runs in the code window while state.winnr points elsewhere under the tab host; hover() is called outside a coroutine so session:request returns nil and the float is skipped silently; the float opens but is placed off-screen (util/float.lua caps width at the owner's columns, and b5584fc switched anchoring to screencol()). Reproduce in the user's real config, not --clean, and add a message on the empty-result path so it is never silent.
acceptance_criteria: <leader>de opens the hover float in normal mode on the word under the cursor and in visual mode on the selection, from the code window and while the Scopes tree is focused, under the tab host. Failure modes produce a message instead of silence.
notes:
probe
2026-09-15: at least part of this is dv-kux. The keymap fires and a float opens; the expression is what fails. With the cursor in the Scopes tree, expand('<cexpr>') picks a type name out of the rendered value and delve rejects it. Re-check from a code window once dv-kux lands.

title: Scopes tree: expansion leaves stale/closed folds in the dap-view window
description: Expanding a node in the Scopes tree renders part of the subtree inside a closed fold instead of showing it. Seen live with debugpy on dap-playground/main.py: after expanding 'root' (Level1) and its 'inner', a closed fold line appears mid-tree reading '+---- 37 lines: special variables' and swallows the rest of the subtree. Navigating/expanding around it behaves erratically.
design: The window uses foldmethod=indent via the render/tree 'fold' config, with a custom foldtext in lua/dap-view/tree/fold.lua. The screenshot shows Neovim's DEFAULT foldtext ('+--- N lines:'), so either foldtext is not applied to that window or the fold comes from options leaking in from the user's global foldmethod/foldexpr (treesitter). Also suspect foldlevel: freshly rendered deeper lines inherit a level above foldlevel and come back closed after a re-render. Check views/options.lua, tree/fold.lua, and whether the render path resets folds (a synchronous parse + zv/zR equivalent) after rewriting buffer lines.
acceptance_criteria: Expanding a node always reveals its children unfolded. No default-format fold line ever appears in the dap-view window. Folding a node shows the fork's own foldtext (name + 'N children'). Headless regression case under both hosts.
